transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Rodriguez (CTO, Aurora), Mark Davis (ML Eng), Priya Singh (DevOps), Elliot (Product)

Topics: quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, SOC2/KMS, networking/VPC, benchmarks

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, this is Samir our solutions engineer, want to kick off with a quick intros and then hear what you're evaluating for Aurora Tech.
00:18 - Lena: Hi all, I'm Lena CTO, we are building a contextual search and chat assistant for our internal knowledge base and customer support. Main goals: fast iteration, low cost for inference, and enterprise controls for data.
00:30 - Mark: Hey, Mark here on infra/ML, curious about latency for short-chats and also token costs for heavy query loads.
00:45 - Priya: Priya, we run private VPCs and strict egress policies; need to understand network requirements and SSO.
01:02 - Maya: Great, thanks. Quick high level — Redwood offers the hosted API for fastest time-to-value, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and private deploy if you need VPC/on-prem. For a PLG quickstart we usually recommend starting hosted with free credits so you can get to first token in hours.
01:21 - Samir: I can show how the quickstart works — SDK, curl, time-to-first-token typically under 30 minutes if you have API keys and a test prompt set. We also have prebuilt templates for embeddings and chat.
01:40 - Mark: So free credits — what's the quota? And is there any rate limiting we should plan around?
01:50 - Maya: The credit amount varies by account but typical quickstart is a few hundred USD equivalent to exercise both embeddings and chat. Rate limits are configurable; out of the box there are soft limits but we can increase for a pilot.
02:10 - Lena: For security, do you have SOC 2 and audit logs? Also KMS/HSM?
02:18 - Samir: Yes SOC 2, we have audit logs in the console, and for private/deployments we support customer KMS integrations. Hosted supports encryption at rest and transit and we provide options for customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private.
02:40 - Priya: If we do hosted, can we keep data from being used to train models? That's a hard requirement.
02:48 - Maya: Absolutely, we have data handling options — we can opt out of any downstream training and set retention policies; for regulated workloads we often recommend Dedicated or Private for more isolation but hosted with contractual protections can work.
03:05 - Mark: From a performance standpoint, what's the typical p95 latency for chat messages on hosted? We're aiming for sub-300ms for short responses if possible.
03:16 - Samir: p95 depends on model choice and batching — for small models and short sequences we often see 100-200ms p95 on our optimized runtime; larger models or longer sequences push that up. We can share detailed perf profiles.
03:35 - Lena: So cost/latency tradeoff — is there an easy way to test multiple models and quantization profiles?
03:45 - Samir: Yes, the platform has a model catalog and you can switch variants; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings for your workload. For the quickstart we'll set up a small benchmark using your sample prompts.
04:02 - Elliot: Onboarding — how long from signup to first token?
04:08 - Maya: Typically under an hour if you use the quickstart guide and SDK; under 24 hours if you need SSO or enterprise set up. We'll provision free credits and send the onboarding link.
04:25 - Priya: Our infra team needs to know if the hosted API requires egress to US regions — data residency is sensitive for some of our customers in EU.
04:36 - Maya: We have region options; hosted can be routed to EU regions for data residency; Dedicated and Private give you more explicit control. We'll capture your residency requirements as an action item.
05:00 - Mark: For dedicated, what's the minimum commit and lead time?
05:08 - Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity — usually monthly or annual commits. Lead time depends on capacity but prototype pools can be provisioned in ~2-3 weeks; for strict SLAs it can be longer. For evaluation we recommend hosted plus a short dedicated pilot.
05:28 - Lena: We might start hosted quickstart and then go to dedicated if throughput requires it.
05:34 - Samir: That path is common. Also important: we support canary rollouts and model pinning so you can control model versions for prod.
06:00 - Mark: Network — what ports/ips do we need to whitelist?
06:08 - Samir: Standard HTTPS egress to our API endpoints; for Private/Dedicated there are options for VPC peering or private links. We'll send exact network ranges.
06:24 - Priya: SSO — SAML? Okta?
06:28 - Maya: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC and common providers like Okta. We'll need your IdP metadata for enterprise setup.
06:42 - Mark: Can we run local benchmarks? Like run a few thousand prompts to measure tail latency and token costs.
06:50 - Samir: Yes we'll supply a benchmark plan and script. For heavy workloads we recommend enabling KV cache/prefix caching for sessions to reduce per-token compute.
07:08 - Lena: How are embeddings priced vs chat?
07:12 - Maya: Embeddings usually priced per-vector unit; chat/generation is per-token. We'll include estimates based on your expected QPS.
07:30 - Elliot: Any known gotchas moving from hosted to dedicated? We want minimal changes to code.
07:36 - Samir: The API is consistent across modes; changing endpoints and credentials is usually the only change. We'll help with migration scripts.
07:50 - Priya: If we went private on-prem, what does the support model look like?
07:56 - Maya: Private comes with enterprise licensing and a support tier. We offer an on-prem package and can run in air-gapped environments with customer-managed keys.
08:12 - Mark: Are there examples of other customers doing PLG quickstarts and then moving to dedicated?
08:18 - Maya: Yes—common pattern is hosted PLG, pilot with dedicated for peak workload, and optionally private for regulated data. We can share anonymized case studies.
08:32 - Lena: Ok let's talk about short-term success criteria: within 2 weeks we want a working demo, within 4 weeks a performance baseline, and a cost estimate.
08:45 - Maya: Sounds reasonable. For the 2-week demo we will provision free credits, provide quickstart docs, and Samir will help with the benchmark script.
09:00 - Samir: I'll draft a test plan — will include 1) small chat latency test, 2) embeddings recall test, 3) cost projection. Mark, can you share typical prompt distributions?
09:10 - Mark: I'll send a sample 200 prompt set and expected QPS range (50-200 QPS for initial).
09:18 - Pause / brief audio artifacts
09:25 - Priya: One more on compliance — we need proof of SOC2 and a diagram of audit logs for Prod.
09:32 - Maya: We'll send SOC2 attestation and sample audit log screenshots; dedicated customers can get longer retention.
09:45 - Mark: Any regulatory certification for EU? Data residency is our main ask.
09:50 - Samir: We have EU regions and compliance options; we'll capture details.
10:05 - Lena: OK let's get concrete. Maya, please send pricing and onboarding, Samir prepare bench plan, Priya will provide network and SSO info.
10:14 - Maya: Yep I'll email the onboarding link with credits and the quickstart doc. Samir will follow-up with benchmarks.
10:21 - Samir: For the benchmark, recommended models: a small open model and a Redwood-curated mid model to compare latency/cost. We'll also test quantized variants.
10:34 - Mark: Onbell — sorry, on model variants, are there recommended quantization settings that balance perf and quality?
10:40 - Samir: Yes we have standard quant profiles; Redwood Optimize can recommend ones per workload. For many use cases 4-bit or 8-bit quant yields good perf with minimal quality drop.
10:56 - Lena: Anything else on contractual terms? For hosted we need a short data protection addendum.
11:02 - Maya: We'll include a DPA and standard terms; for enterprise we'll surface additional clauses.
11:12 - Elliot: One small thing — can the quickstart include a sample UI template for internal chat?
11:16 - Maya: Yes we have starter templates we can share.
11:25 - Closing recap: Maya: action items are sending credits and quickstart, Samir bench plan, Priya network + SSO. We'll schedule a follow-up in a week to check progress and a deeper SE demo if needed.
11:40 - Lena: Thanks everyone, looking forward to trying it out.
11:45 - End of meeting

Notes: transcript has minor auto-transcription errors and occasional speaker label drift. References: quickstart guide (link sent post-call), SOC2 doc (link), benchmark template (link).
